subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When the native Codex relay fails before the current tool invocation, should generic `before_tool_call` policy be an approved equivalent enforcement path, or must execution remain blocked until the relay is refreshed?
rationale: Both approaches can recover the user workflow, but choosing whether relay unavailability may cross into generic policy fallback defines the permanent native-tool security boundary and cannot be inferred safely from unit tests.

options.title: Accept Guarded Fallback After Proof
options.body: Allow the current fallback only after exact-head runtime evidence shows all relevant policy and approval enforcement still runs after restart recovery.

options.title: Require Relay Recovery
options.body: Keep unavailable native approvals fail-closed and refresh or re-register the current relay before permitting the tool call.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Fallback After Proof
recommendation.body: Allow the current fallback only after exact-head runtime evidence shows all relevant policy and approval enforcement still runs after restart recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly related merged fallback contract and its fail-closed exceptions were authored and merged in this area by steipete.
